healthcareSystem: US healthcare system. Puerto Rico operates under FDA regulations and US medical standards. Hospitals and pharmacies follow the same rules as the US mainland. Medicare and Medicaid apply. Most US health insurance plans are accepted.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is comparable to the US mainland. San Juan has excellent hospitals and specialists. Rural areas and smaller islands have more limited facilities. US-trained doctors are common. English is widely spoken in medical settings.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-9pm daily. Walgreens and CVS locations open extended hours, some 24/7 in San Juan. Walmart pharmacies also available.
pharmacyTips: US pharmacy chains (Walgreens, CVS) are widespread. US prescriptions are valid. Insurance co-pays apply as on the mainland. Over-the-counter medications are the same as in the US. Spanish is the primary language but English is widely understood.
prescriptionRules: Same as US mainland. FDA regulations apply. US prescriptions are valid. Controlled substances follow DEA scheduling. Pharmacists are licensed under the same standards.

restrictedMeds.name: DEA Schedule II substances
restrictedMeds.note: Same as US mainland. Opioids, amphetamines require valid prescription. DEA regulations apply.

restrictedMeds.name: DEA Schedule III-V substances
restrictedMeds.note: Require valid US prescription. Same regulations as mainland.

bringDocumentation: US prescription medications travel freely between mainland and Puerto Rico. No customs or special documentation needed. Carry medications in original pharmacy bottles as a general best practice.

travelInsurance.tips: US health insurance works in Puerto Rico. Medicare is accepted. If you have US insurance, no additional coverage needed. International travelers without US insurance should get travel insurance as US healthcare is expensive.

vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required. Same recommendations as US mainland travel. Routine vaccinations should be up to date. Zika was previously a concern — check current CDC advisories.

waterNotes: Tap water is treated to US EPA standards and safe to drink throughout Puerto Rico. After severe weather events, local authorities may issue boil-water advisories — check local news if traveling during hurricane season.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards follow US FDA regulations. Restaurant hygiene is well-regulated. Street food (alcapurrias, bacalaítos, piñones) from popular stalls is generally safe. Seafood is fresh and abundant. No special precautions needed beyond normal food safety practices.
medicalTourismNote: Puerto Rico is not a typical medical tourism destination as it follows US pricing. However, some procedures may cost less than on the mainland while maintaining US quality standards.
sources: US Department of Health and Human Services
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Puerto Rico. US healthcare system, 911 emergency, pharmacy info, and health tips for San Juan and the island.

hospitals.name: Centro Médico de Puerto Rico (Puerto Rico Medical Center)
hospitals.notes: Largest medical complex in the Caribbean. Trauma center. Level 1 trauma care. Multiple specialized departments.

hospitals.name: Hospital HIMA San Pablo - Bayamón
hospitals.notes: Major private hospital. Emergency services 24/7. Modern facilities.

hospitals.name: Ashford Presbyterian Community Hospital
hospitals.notes: Located in the heart of the tourist area. Convenient for visitors staying in Condado/Isla Verde. Full emergency department.

hospitals.name: Hospital Pavia Santurce
hospitals.notes: Private hospital in the San Juan metro area. Emergency and specialty services.

dentalCare.availability: Excellent dental care available throughout Puerto Rico. Many US-trained dentists. San Juan has numerous dental offices and specialists.
dentalCare.costRange: $50-100 for consultation; $100-250 for fillings; $150-300 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Dental care follows US standards. Costs may be slightly lower than mainland US. Many dentists are bilingual. US dental insurance often accepted.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Emergency dental care available at hospital emergency departments and many private dental offices accept walk-ins. Ashford Presbyterian area has several dental practices near the tourist zone.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Widely available. Many bilingual therapists throughout the island.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services follow US standards. 988 crisis line is available. Many therapists are bilingual English/Spanish. Telehealth options widely available.

accessibilityInfo.overview: ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) applies in Puerto Rico. Major hotels, restaurants, and attractions are required to meet ADA standards. Old San Juan has cobblestone streets that can be challenging.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospitals are ADA compliant with wheelchair access, elevators, and accessible facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses (AMA) have wheelchair lifts. Taxis available. Ride-sharing services operate. Rental cars with hand controls can be arranged.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Old San Juan's historic district has uneven cobblestone streets and steep hills — challenging for wheelchair users. Beach boardwalks in Condado and Isla Verde are more accessible. Many attractions offer accessible options.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask requirements. Same as US mainland guidelines.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at pharmacies (CVS, Walgreens), urgent care centers, and hospitals.
covidStatus.notes: Puerto Rico follows US CDC guidelines. No special requirements for travel from the US mainland.

insuranceClaimProcess: Same as US mainland. Hospitals and pharmacies process insurance claims directly. US insurance cards accepted. Co-pays and deductibles apply as usual. International visitors should keep all receipts for travel insurance claims.

commonCosts.note: US healthcare pricing applies. Costs are similar to mainland US, sometimes slightly lower. With US insurance, co-pays typically apply. Without insurance, costs can be very high.

medicalEvacuation.note: Puerto Rico has good hospitals that handle most cases. Medical flights to mainland US are available for specialized care. Air ambulance services operate regular routes to Miami and other mainland cities.
